### Bible Pathways 02/23/2002
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-02-or-23-or-2002-1127466.html
Passage: Numbers 23:5
Points:
- Balak offered wealth and honor to persuade Balaam to place a curse on Israel.
- Balaam initially recognized his inability to pronounce a curse on a people God had blessed.
- Greed for status and riches ultimately caused Balaam to compromise his obedience.
- Though constrained by God to speak blessings, he later plotted to entice Israel into sin.
- Desiring a peaceful end like the righteous is empty without living in obedience to God.

### Read the Bible: Numbers 23, Psalms 64-65, Isaiah 13, 1 Peter 1
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numbers-23-psalms-64-65-isaiah-13-1-peter-1/
Passage: Numbers 23:1-12
Points:
- Balaam recognizes he cannot manipulate God or control the divine words he receives.
- The oracle establishes that a prophet cannot curse or denounce what the Lord has not cursed.
- Israel is portrayed as a distinct covenant community set apart from surrounding nations.
- Balak reflects superstitious religion that tries to use God to dispense blessings and curses.
- God’s sovereign blessing over His redeemed people provides an enduring foundation for confidence and hope.
